case.title: Host check for rule matching

provenance.provenance_notes: Reconstructed from a real werkzeug bug fix in MapAdapter.build(): the pre-fix condition was `not force_external and (subdomain_matching or host_matching) and ((subdomain_matching and domain_part==subdomain) or (host_matching and host==server_name))` -- a compound AND-chain with no branch for 'neither subdomain nor host matching is configured'. The fix rewrote it to `not force_external and (not (subdomain_matching or host_matching) or (subdomain_matching and domain_part==subdomain) or (host_matching and host==server_name))`, adding the missing OR-branch so an unscoped rule still matches. No werkzeug identifiers, file paths, or code are reproduced -- variable names and surrounding code are invented, but the three-term compound-condition structure and the specific missing-OR-branch mechanism are preserved. The diff below is the reverse of the historical fix: it removes the added OR-branch and restores the AND-chain, reintroducing the original defect.

diff: def matches_context(domain_locked, host_locked, force_external, domain_ok, host_ok):

ground_truth.explanation: The fixed form is 'not force_external and (not (domain_locked or host_locked) or (domain_locked and domain_ok) or (host_locked and host_ok))': when neither domain_locked nor host_locked is set, the middle term is True, so an unscoped rule still matches. The defect replaces that OR-structure with 'not force_external and (domain_locked or host_locked) and (...)': now, when neither lock is set, '(domain_locked or host_locked)' is False and the whole expression is False -- an unscoped rule silently stops matching, even though nothing about it was ever supposed to require host/subdomain scoping. This is a missing-branch/De Morgan-style compound-boolean bug, not a single inverted flag.
